title: Graff wins Portimão as G-Drive takes the LMP2 title
dek: Graff's Oreca #40 won the 4 Hours of Portimão by 38 seconds after United's Ligier was penalised for pit-lane speeding, and fourth place secured G-Drive's LMP2 title from third on the grid.

chapters.title: A new circuit for a title decider
text: The European Le Mans Series ended its 2017 season at the Algarve circuit near Portimão on 22 October, seven years after its predecessor last raced there. The finale replaced the usual date at Estoril, and 35 cars entered, with 12 of them in LMP2, the first year of the new-generation prototypes: Oreca 07, Ligier JS P217 and Dallara P217 were all on the grid. It was a round where all three class titles were still open, and in LMP2 the fight was between two teams that had split the season. G-Drive Racing by DragonSpeed arrived 18 points clear on 98, with the #22 Oreca of Rojas and Roussel and a third driver, Hirakawa, who had missed two rounds because of his racing commitments in Japan and so was not part of the drivers' title equation. The team had won only once, at Monza, and finished second at each of the other four rounds, consistency rather than dominance carrying it to the final race.

United Autosports' #32 Ligier of Owen, de Sadeleer and Albuquerque had won at Silverstone and the Red Bull Ring but had slipped to sixth at Monza and fifth at Le Castellet. The crew needed to win and then hope for trouble for the leaders, since a top-five or top-six finish for G-Drive was enough to end the argument. Graff, with the #40 Oreca of Allen, Bradley and Yacaman, had won at Spa and sat third on 61 points with an outside chance of the runner-up place, while SMP Racing's Dallara, winner at Le Castellet, was fifth in the table after missing the first two rounds.

The wider LMP2 picture was noisy. A week earlier the ACO had confirmed one-off 'Joker' updates for the Ligier, Dallara and Riley, but not for the Oreca, and Oreca's president said the company felt unfairly penalised. G-Drive had also used the Tuesday test to give Audi factory driver Nico Müller eleven laps in an LMP2 for the first time ahead of his Shanghai WEC debut with the team, on a day of mixed weather. On track DragonSpeed's #21 Oreca topped Friday practice through Lapierre with a 1:34.182, and Hirakawa went quickest of the weekend in Saturday morning's session with a 1:34.034 for the points leaders.

chapters.title: Panis Barthez steals pole
text: Qualifying was a ten-minute session cut short by a red flag when Pizzitola spun the Algarve Pro Racing Ligier #25 into the gravel at Turn 16 after about three minutes, leaving seven on the clock at the restart. Hirakawa set the early pace for G-Drive with a 1:34.235, but Nathanaël Berthon beat it with a 1:33.575 in the Michelin-shod Panis Barthez Ligier #23. It was the team's first pole of the year, its previous best grid slot having been fourth at the Red Bull Ring, and the first for a Ligier P217 in LMP2 competition that season. Berthon called it 'mega' and credited a long run of work across the season.

Nicolas Lapierre, who had spun at Turn 14 earlier in the run, recovered to take second for the #21 DragonSpeed Oreca with a 1:34.090, 0.515 seconds off pole, which pushed the championship leaders onto the second row. Hirakawa held third, and the Graff #39 of Guibbert was fourth on 1:34.240, five thousandths slower than the points leaders. Filipe Albuquerque put the United Ligier #32 fifth on 1:34.551, ahead of the Idec Ligier #28 of Chatin on 1:34.746 and the Cetilar Villorba Corse Dallara #47 of Belicchi on 1:35.110. SMP's Dallara #27 of Isaakyan was eighth and the Graff #40 of Bradley ninth.

With the grid set, G-Drive needed only a steady race. Albuquerque, racing at his home circuit, said United would take risks and go for the win, since the team had little to lose and wanted to make G-Drive feel the pressure.

chapters.title: De Sadeleer goes from fifth to first
text: The race started at 13:00 and the United Ligier #32 moved immediately. Hugo de Sadeleer, starting from fifth, climbed through the field in the opening stint and took the lead from Fabien Barthez in the pole-sitting Panis Barthez Ligier. A first Safety Car then slowed the field when Henrik Hedman put the DragonSpeed Oreca #21 into the gravel at Turn 5. Behind the leaders Léo Roussel held third in the title-chasing G-Drive Oreca, with Sernagiotto fourth for Cetilar Villorba Corse in the #47 Dallara and Yacaman fifth in the Graff #40. At the restart Roussel went past Barthez into Turn 1 to move to second, and Yacaman gained places too.

chapters.title: Four cars lead, then the penalty
text: At the two-hour mark de Sadeleer led and Roussel was in the position to win the title, 44 seconds behind. The race then opened up. During the first round of stops Egor Orudzhev briefly put the SMP Racing Dallara #27 in front, and as the middle phase wore on the Ligier #32, the G-Drive Oreca, the Graff Oreca and the SMP car all took a turn at the front. Shortly before halfway James Allen took the lead for Graff by passing de Sadeleer at Turn 14, and the United car lost a few seconds in the pits when it would not fire up at its next stop.

The race turned on a pit-lane offence. With less than 80 minutes remaining, Will Owen, leading in the #32, was given a stop-and-hold penalty plus 55 seconds for speeding in the pit lane. It cost the car the lead and dropped it to third, and with it United's chance of the title, since G-Drive was running comfortably in the top three. Graff's own afternoon was not trouble-free: the fuel tank was short by roughly 20 litres at each stop, which forced an extra visit to the pits late on.

chapters.title: Bradley wins, Albuquerque takes second
text: In the closing stages Paul Petit spun the Graff #39 at the last corner and speared across the track into the barriers at the end of the pit lane, blocking the entrance. The marshals cleared it under local yellows. Richard Bradley, now in the #40 Oreca, caught and passed the United Ligier to take the lead and kept it to the flag. Isaakyan was second in the SMP Dallara until five minutes from the end, when Filipe Albuquerque, driving in front of his home crowd, passed him to put the United Ligier back into second.

Bradley won by 38.169 seconds from the #32, with the Dallara of Isaakyan and Orudzhev third, 59.254 seconds behind the winner. Hirakawa finished fourth in the G-Drive Oreca, 1.944 seconds from the SMP car and well clear of the fifth-placed Cetilar Dallara, which finished a lap down, as did Panis Barthez in sixth after starting from pole. DragonSpeed's #21 recovered from its gravel trip to ninth, two laps down, with Hanley setting the race's fastest lap of 1:35.048. For Graff it was a second win of the season after Spa; Bradley said the stressful final stint was played out without knowing for certain that the car would make the flag.

chapters.title: A first title for G-Drive and DragonSpeed
text: Fourth place was enough. G-Drive Racing by DragonSpeed won the LMP2 teams' title, and Rojas and Roussel took the drivers' crown, after a season of one win, at Monza, and second places at Silverstone, the Red Bull Ring, Le Castellet and Spa. It was G-Drive's second ELMS LMP2 title in a row, DragonSpeed's first international championship and the first for the Oreca 07 chassis. Team principal Elton Julian praised the team effort and said the whole story of how the programme was put together would come out one day. Roussel called it the best moment of his life, and the team ended up in the swimming pool outside the media centre. Rojas said winning in Europe had been a dream since he left racing in America.

The ELMS awards on Sunday evening honoured several LMP2 names: Cetilar Villorba Corse was named Team of the Year after moving up from LMP3 with the Dallara P217, Hugo de Sadeleer won Rookie of the Year, and DragonSpeed's Hedman was named Gentleman Driver of the Year. United's trio, Owen, de Sadeleer and Albuquerque, finished the season as runners-up to G-Drive.

Graff's win gave Dunlop its 17th ELMS victory in a row, and G-Drive's title was the 10th for the tyre manufacturer in the ELMS LMP2 championship, the ninth in a row. G-Drive's title also brought the team the sole Le Mans entry through the LMP2 results, one of the automatic places confirmed that Sunday alongside entries for United, JMW and TF Sport.

The 2018 LMP2 picture already had a new element, with the Joker updates for the Ligier, Dallara and Riley still to be homologated through wind-tunnel tests. G-Drive's own next step was the World Endurance Championship round at Shanghai, where Nico Müller was set to drive its Oreca after his Portimão test laps.

facts.v: Nathanaël Berthon took pole in the Panis Barthez Ligier #23 with 1:33.575, 0.515 s clear of the DragonSpeed Oreca #21.
